{{Short description|Endofunctor on the category of simplicial sets}}
{{Other uses|Subdivision (disambiguation)}}[[File:Barycentric_subdivision.svg|thumb|Process of subdivision of the standard <math>2</math>-simplex <math>\Delta^2</math>: The partially ordered set <math>[2]=\{0,1,2\}</math> with <math>0\leq 1</math>, <math>1\leq 2</math> and <math>0\leq 2</math> forms a triangle, while the partially ordered set <math>s([2])=\{\{0\},\{1\},\{2\},\{0,1\},\{1,2\},\{0,2\},\{0,1,2\}\}</math> forms its subdivision with <math>\{0\}</math>, <math>\{1\}</math> and <math>\{2\}</math> being the original triangle, <math>\{0,1\}</math>, <math>\{1,2\}</math> and <math>\{0,2\}</math> subdividing the edges and <math>\{0,1,2\}</math> subdividing the face.]]
In [[higher category theory]] in [[mathematics]], the '''subdivision''' of [[Simplicial set|simplicial sets]] ('''subdivision functor''' or '''Sd functor''') is an [[endofunctor]] on the [[category of simplicial sets]]. It refines the structure of simplicial sets in a purely [[Combinatorics|combinatorical]] way without changing constructions like the [[Geometric realization functor|geometric realization]]. Furthermore, the subdivision of simplicial sets plays an important role in the [[Extension (simplicial set)|extension]] of simplicial sets [[right adjoint]] to it.

== Definition ==
For a [[partially ordered set]] <math>I</math>, let <math>s(I)</math> be the set of non-empty finite [[Totally ordered set|totally ordered subsets]], which itself is partially ordered by inclusion. Every partially ordered set can be considered as a category. Postcomposition with the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]] <math>N\colon
\mathbf{Cat}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> defines the subdivision functor <math>\operatorname{Sd}\colon
\Delta\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> on the [[simplex category]] by:

: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n)
:=N(s([n])).
</math>

On the full category of simplicial sets, the subdivision functor <math>\operatorname{Sd}\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math>, similar to the [[Geometric realization functor|geometric realization]], is defined through an extension by colimits. For a simplicial set <math>X</math>, one therefore has:<ref>Goerss & Jardine 1999, S. 183</ref>

: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(X)
:=\varinjlim_{\Delta^n\rightarrow X}\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n).
</math>

With the [[Greatest element and least element|maximum]] <math>\max\colon
s(I)\rightarrow I</math>, which in partially ordered sets neither has to exist nor has to be unique, which both holds in totally ordered sets, there is a [[natural transformation]] <math>a\colon
\operatorname{Sd}\Rightarrow\operatorname{Id}</math> by extension. In particular there is a canonical morphism <math>a_X\colon
\operatorname{Sd}(X)\rightarrow X</math> for every simplicial set <math>X</math>.

== Sd∞ functor ==
For a simplicial set <math>X</math>, the canonical morphism <math>a_X\colon
\operatorname{Sd}(X)
\rightarrow X</math> indudes an <math>\mathbb{N}</math>-shaped [[cocone]] <math>\ldots\rightarrow\operatorname{Sd}^3(X)\rightarrow\operatorname{Sd}^2(X)\rightarrow\operatorname{Sd}(X)\rightarrow X</math>, whose [[colimit]] is denoted:

: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}^\infty(X)
:=\varprojlim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\operatorname{Sd}^n(X).
</math>

Since limit and colimit are switched, there is '''no''' adjunction <math>\operatorname{Sd}^\infty\dashv\operatorname{Ex}^\infty</math> with the [[Ex∞ functor]].

The natural transformation <math>a\colon\operatorname{Sd}\Rightarrow\operatorname{Id}</math> induces a natural transformation <math>\alpha\colon
\operatorname{Sd}^\infty\Rightarrow\operatorname{Id}</math>. In particular, there is a canonical morphism <math>\alpha_X\colon
\operatorname{Sd}^\infty(X)\rightarrow X</math> for every simplicial set <math>X</math>.

== Examples ==
Directly from the definition, one has:<ref>Cisinski 2019, 3.8.6.</ref>

: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^0)
=\Delta^0,
</math>
: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^1)
=\Lambda_2^2.
</math>
Since <math>
\partial\Delta^1
\cong\Delta^0+\Delta^0
</math>, it is fixed under (infinite) subdivision:
: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(\partial\Delta^1)
=\partial\Delta^1,
</math>
: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}^\infty(\partial\Delta^1)
=\partial\Delta^1.
</math>

== Properties ==

* For every simplicial set <math>X</math>, the canonical morphism <math>a_X\colon
\operatorname{Sd}(X)\rightarrow X</math> is a [[Weak equivalence (homotopy theory)|weak homotopy equivalence]].<ref>Cisinski 2019,  Proposition 3.1.19.</ref>
* The subdivision functor <math>\operatorname{Sd}</math> preserves [[Monomorphism|monomorphisms]] and weak homotopy equivalences (which follows directly from the preceding property and their 2-of-3 property) as well as [[Anodyne extension|anodyne extensions]] in combination,<ref>Cisinski 2019, Proposition 3.1.18.</ref> hence cofibrations and trivial cofibrations of the [[Kan–Quillen model structure]]. This makes the adjunction <math>\operatorname{Sd}\dashv\operatorname{Ex}</math> even into a [[Quillen adjunction]] <math>\operatorname{Sd}\colon
\mathbf{sSet}_\mathrm{KQ}\rightleftarrows\mathbf{sSet}_\mathrm{KQ}\colon
\operatorname{Ex}</math>.
* For a partially ordered set <math>I</math>, one has with the nerve:<ref>Cisinski 2019, Lemma 3.1.25.</ref>
*: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(N(I))
\cong N(s(I)).
</math>
: Using <math>I=[n]</math> with <math>\Delta^n=N([n])</math> results in the definition again.
* Let <math>\Phi_k^n</math> be the set of non-empty subsets of <math>[n]</math>, which don't contain the complement of <math>\{k\}</math>, and let <math>\partial\Phi^n</math> be the set of non-empty proper subsets of <math>[n]</math>, then:<ref>Cisinski 2019, Lemma 3.1.26.</ref>
*: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(\Lambda_k^n)
\cong N(\Phi_k^n),
</math>
*: <math>
\operatorname{Sd}(\partial\Delta^n)
\cong N(\partial\Phi^n).
</math>
* The subdivision functor preserves the geometric realization. For a simplicial set <math>X</math>, one has:<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Lurie |first=Jacob |author-link=Jacob Lurie |title=Kerodon, Proposition 3.3.3.7. |url=https://kerodon.net/tag/00YB |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=kerodon.net |language=en}}</ref>
*: <math>
|\operatorname{Sd}(X)|
\cong|X|.
</math>

: Since both functors are defined through extension by colimits, it is sufficient to show <math>
|\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n)|
=|\Delta^n|
</math>.<ref>Goerss & Jardine 1999, S. 182</ref>
